This is the R twin of the Python guide
[`distributions-for-actuaries-claim-size.md`](distributions-for-actuaries-claim-size.md).
It recomputes the examples and problems of chapters 2, 5 and 6 of CAS
Monograph 2, *Distributions for Actuaries* by David Bahnemann (2015), with the
same sections and numbers. Read the Python guide for the discussion of each
result. The companion R guide,
[`distributions-for-actuaries-counts-aggregates.qmd`](distributions-for-actuaries-counts-aggregates.qmd),
covers chapters 3 and 4.

`R/prospicio/tests/test-guides.R` requires each chunk to print exactly the text
under it (a table prints as its labels and formatted cells). `book` is the
monograph's printed value, a literal in the code. In tables with one row per
grid point, each row marked ", book" is the monograph's value under
prospicio's. This guide minimizes with R's
`optim()`, the Python guide with SciPy's Nelder–Mead; both find the same minima
to the printed digits.

## 1. Translating the parameters

| Monograph | Its formula | prospicio (R) |
|---|---|---|
| gamma (α, β), β a scale | mean αβ | `gamma_distribution(α, β)` |
| exponential β | mean β | `gamma_distribution(1, β)` |
| lognormal (μ, σ) | log X normal (μ, σ) | `lognormal(μ, σ)` |
| Weibull (β, δ) | F = 1 − exp(−(x/β)^δ) | `weibull_distribution(shape = δ, scale = β)` |
| Pareto (α, β), the "shifted" one used in all examples | F = 1 − (β/(x+β))^α, from 0 | `generalized_pareto(1/α, β/α)`, or `burr_distribution(α, 1, β)` |
| classical Pareto (γ, α) | F = 1 − (γ/x)^α, from γ | `pareto(γ, α)` |

The monograph's Pareto starts at zero (a Lomax). prospicio's `pareto()` starts at
a threshold. `limited_second_moment` builds E[X²; l] as `layer_variance +
layer^2` from a `truncated_distribution()` with no bounds. `surv()` is `1 - cdf()`. `book_table()` and
`grid_table()` are the guide's table helpers.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(prospicio)
library(gt)

shifted_pareto <- function(alpha, beta) generalized_pareto(1 / alpha, beta / alpha)
surv <- function(sev, x) 1 - cdf(sev, x)
limited_second_moment <- function(sev, limit) {
  t <- truncated_distribution(sev)
  layer_variance(t, limit, 0) + layer(t, limit, 0)^2
}
layer_second_moment <- function(sev, limit, attachment) {
  t <- truncated_distribution(sev)
  layer_variance(t, limit, attachment) + layer(t, limit, attachment)^2
}
num <- function(x, digits = 0) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",")

row <- function(label, book, ours, digits = 0) list(label, book, ours, digits)
book_table <- function(rows, title, subtitle = NULL) {
  frame <- data.frame(item = vapply(rows, function(r) r[[1]], ""),
                      book = vapply(rows, function(r) r[[2]], 0),
                      prospicio = vapply(rows, function(r) r[[3]], 0))
  digits <- vapply(rows, function(r) r[[4]], 0)
  table <- gt(frame, rowname_col = "item")
  for (places in sort(unique(digits))) {
    table <- fmt_number(table, columns = c(book, prospicio), rows = which(digits == places), decimals = places)
  }
  table |> sub_missing(missing_text = "") |> tab_header(title, subtitle)
}
# One measure: book and prospicio columns. Several: rows alternate prospicio and ", book".
# Each measure is list(name, book values, prospicio values, decimals).
grid_table <- function(stub, index, measures, title, subtitle = NULL) {
  at <- if (is.numeric(index)) formatC(index, format = "f", digits = 0, big.mark = ",") else index
  if (length(measures) == 1) {
    m <- measures[[1]]
    table <- gt(data.frame(at = at, book = m[[2]], prospicio = m[[3]]), rowname_col = "at") |>
      tab_spanner(m[[1]], columns = c(book, prospicio)) |>
      fmt_number(columns = c(book, prospicio), decimals = m[[4]])
  } else {
    frame <- data.frame(at = as.vector(rbind(at, paste0(at, ", book"))))
    for (m in measures) frame[[m[[1]]]] <- as.vector(rbind(m[[3]], m[[2]]))
    table <- gt(frame, rowname_col = "at")
    for (m in measures) table <- fmt_number(table, columns = all_of(m[[1]]), decimals = m[[4]])
  }
  table |> tab_stubhead(stub) |> sub_missing(missing_text = "") |> tab_header(title, subtitle)
}

p <- shifted_pareto(2, 3000)
closed_form <- 3000 / (2 - 1) * (1 - 3000 / (8000 + 3000))
cat(sprintf("E[X; 8,000] of Pareto (2; 3,000): book 2,182, closed form %s, prospicio %s, Burr %s\n",
            num(closed_form, 2), num(lev(p, 8000), 2), num(lev(burr_distribution(2, 1, 3000), 8000), 2)))
```

```text
E[X; 8,000] of Pareto (2; 3,000): book 2,182, closed form 2,181.82, prospicio 2,181.82, Burr 2,181.82
```

## 2. Limited expected values

```{r}
#| label: lev
x <- gamma_distribution(1, 250)
rows <- list(row("Ex 2.4 E[X; 400]", 199.53, lev(x, 400), 2),
             row("Ex 2.4 E[X^2; 400]", 59384, limited_second_moment(x, 400)))

x <- pareto(1000, 3)
rows <- c(rows, list(row("P2.1 mean", 1500, mean(x)),
                     row("P2.1 variance", 750000, variance(x)),
                     row("P2.1 Pr{X > 2,000}", 0.1250, survival(x, 2000), 4),
                     row("P2.1 E[X; 2,000]", 1375, lev(x, 2000))))

cases <- list(
  list("P2.17", lognormal(6.3210, 1.6000), c(556, 0.1461, 0.2108, 1023, 9689)),
  list("P2.19", shifted_pareto(3, 4000), c(1040, 0.1866, 0.3254, 1347, 6500))
)
for (case in cases) {
  name <- case[[1]]; x <- case[[2]]; book <- case[[3]]
  s3 <- surv(x, 3000)
  rows <- c(rows, list(
    row(paste(name, "median"), book[1], quantile(x, 0.5)),
    row(paste(name, "Pr{X > 3,000}"), book[2], s3, 4),
    row(paste(name, "Pr{1,000 < X <= 3,000}"), book[3], cdf(x, 3000) - cdf(x, 1000), 4),
    row(paste(name, "E[X; 3,000]"), book[4], lev(x, 3000)),
    row(paste(name, "E[X | X > 3,000]"), book[5], 3000 + stop_loss(x, 3000) / s3)))
}
book_table(rows, "Limited expected values and tail probabilities", "Chapter 2, examples and problems")
```

## 3. Fitting grouped data

Ex 2.7 matches a gamma to the sample moments M1 = 1,555 and M2 = 3,036,875 of
Ex 2.6's 200 claims. The printed scale 397.931 is a slip for 397.974. The
monograph's tables use it, and so do the next chunks:

```{r}
#| label: ex27
M1 <- 1555; M2 <- 3036875
cat(sprintf("alpha %.6f (book 3.907288), beta %.3f (book 397.931)\n", M1^2 / (M2 - M1^2), (M2 - M1^2) / M1))
```

```text
alpha 3.907288 (book 3.907288), beta 397.974 (book 397.931)
```

```{r}
#| label: ex27-fit
CUTS <- c(0, 1000, 1500, 2000, 2500, 3000, Inf)
OBSERVED <- c(42, 61, 47, 26, 14, 10)
cell_probs <- function(sev, cuts) {
  F <- sapply(cuts, function(c) if (c == 0) 0 else if (is.infinite(c)) 1 else cdf(sev, c))
  diff(F)
}
chi_square <- function(sev, cuts = CUTS, observed = OBSERVED) {
  n <- sum(observed)
  e <- n * cell_probs(sev, cuts)
  sum((observed - e)^2 / e)
}
g <- gamma_distribution(3.907288, 397.931)
xs <- c(1000, 1500, 2000, 2500, 3000)
grid_table("x", xs, list(
  list("Pr{X > x}", c(0.7382, 0.4604, 0.2465, 0.1186, 0.0528), surv(g, xs), 4),
  list("E[X; x]", c(924, 1223, 1396, 1484, 1525), sapply(xs, function(x) lev(g, x)), 0)
), "Ex 2.7: the gamma fitted by moments")
```

```text

2,000, book     0.2465    1,396
2,500           0.1186    1,484
2,500, book     0.1186    1,484
3,000           0.0528    1,525
3,000, book     0.0528    1,525
```

Ex 2.8 fits a lognormal by minimum chi-square. At the monograph's lognormal the
statistic is 1.020, not the printed 1.828. The true minimum is lower:

```{r}
#| label: ex28

grid_table("x", xs, list(
  list("Pr{X > x}", c(0.7965, 0.4653, 0.2305, 0.1072, 0.0491), surv(ln, xs), 4),
  list("E[X; x]", c(958, 1273, 1441, 1522, 1559), sapply(xs, function(x) lev(ln, x)), 0)
), "Ex 2.8: the lognormal at the monograph's parameters")
```

1,000, book     0.7965      958
1,500           0.4653    1,273

2,000           0.2305    1,441
2,000, book     0.2305    1,441

```{r}
#| label: ex28-min
min_chi_square <- function(make, start, ...) {
  fit <- optim(start, function(p) chi_square(make(p[1], p[2]), ...), method = "Nelder-Mead",
               control = list(reltol = 1e-14, maxit = 4000))
  list(par = fit$par, value = fit$value)
}
f <- min_chi_square(function(m, s) lognormal(m, abs(s)), c(7.2, 0.5))
g2 <- min_chi_square(function(a, b) gamma_distribution(abs(a), abs(b)), c(4, 400))
book_table(list(row("Ex 2.8 chi-square at the book's parameters", 1.828, chi_square(ln), 3),
                row("Ex 2.8 smallest chi-square", NA_real_, f$value, 3),
                row("Ex 2.8 mu at the smallest", NA_real_, f$par[1], 4),
                row("Ex 2.8 sigma at the smallest", NA_real_, abs(f$par[2]), 4),
                row("P2.16 gamma a", 4.7432, abs(g2$par[1]), 4),
                row("P2.16 gamma b", 337.31, abs(g2$par[2]), 2)),
           "Minimum chi-square fits", "Ex 2.8's lognormal and P2.16's gamma")
```

```text
                                              book  prospicio

Ex 2.8 mu at the smallest                              7.2857
Ex 2.8 sigma at the smallest                           0.4570
P2.16 gamma a                               4.7432     4.7432
P2.16 gamma b                               337.31     337.31
```

Each band's count beside the two fits shows where they differ:

```{r}
#| label: ex26-figure
library(ggplot2, exclude = "layer")   # keeps prospicio's layer()
bands <- factor(c("0-1k", "1-1.5k", "1.5-2k", "2-2.5k", "2.5-3k", "3k+"),
                levels = c("0-1k", "1-1.5k", "1.5-2k", "2-2.5k", "2.5-3k", "3k+"))
least <- min_chi_square(function(m, s) lognormal(m, abs(s)), c(7.2, 0.5))$par
two_fits <- list("gamma, Ex 2.7" = g, "lognormal, least chi-square" = lognormal(least[1], abs(least[2])))
expected <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(two_fits), function(name) {
  data.frame(band = bands, fit = name, claims = 200 * cell_probs(two_fits[[name]], CUTS))
}))
ggplot(expected, aes(band, claims)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = "observed claims"), data = data.frame(band = bands, claims = OBSERVED)) +
  geom_line(aes(colour = fit, group = fit), linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = fit), size = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("observed claims" = "grey75")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "claims in the band", fill = NULL, colour = NULL,
       title = "Ex 2.6: 200 claims by size band, and two fitted distributions") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## 4. Censored and truncated data

Minimum limited-mean distance for the censored samples of Ex 2.10 and P2.39:

```{r}
#| label: censored
min_distance <- function(sizes, empirical, start) {
  distance <- function(p) {
    ln <- lognormal(p[1], abs(p[2]))
    sum((sapply(sizes, function(x) lev(ln, x)) - empirical)^2)
  }
  fit <- optim(start, distance, method = "Nelder-Mead", control = list(reltol = 1e-14, maxit = 4000))
  c(fit$par[1], abs(fit$par[2]))
}
sizes <- c(1000, 5000, 10000, 25000, 50000, 100000, 200000, 300000)
below <- c(729, 1096, 1208, 1326, 1391, 1440, 1468, 1500)
total_below <- c(225138, 1102272, 1918947, 3752091, 6007543, 9234739, 13100561, 22343455)
emp <- (total_below + sizes * (1500 - below)) / 1500
fit_2_10 <- min_distance(sizes, emp, c(7, 2.5))
grid_table("x", sizes, list(
  list("E[X; x]", c(648, 2091, 3239, 5410, 7580, 10168, 13069, 14850),
       sapply(sizes, function(x) lev(lognormal(fit_2_10[1], fit_2_10[2]), x)), 0)
), "Ex 2.10: limited means of the lognormal fitted by minimum distance")
```

```text
           book  prospicio
1,000       648        648
5,000     2,091      2,091
10,000    3,239      3,239
25,000    5,410      5,410
50,000    7,580      7,580
100,000  10,168     10,168
200,000  13,069     13,069
300,000  14,850     14,850
```

```{r}
#| label: censored-p239
sizes <- c(10000, 20000, 30000, 40000, 50000, 60000, 80000, 100000)
counts <- c(78, 27, 21, 15, 12, 10, 8, 7)          # 22 more at the 100,000 limit
mids <- c(5000, 15000, 25000, 35000, 45000, 55000, 70000, 90000)
emp <- (cumsum(counts * mids) + sizes * (200 - cumsum(counts))) / 200
f <- min_distance(sizes, emp, c(9.7, 1.4))
book_table(list(row("Ex 2.10 mu", 6.9852, fit_2_10[1], 4), row("Ex 2.10 sigma", 2.5850, fit_2_10[2], 4),
                row("P2.39 mu", 9.778102, f[1], 4), row("P2.39 sigma", 1.444776, f[2], 4)),
           "Lognormals fitted to censored samples", "Minimum limited-mean distance")
```

```text
                 book  prospicio
Ex 2.10 mu     6.9852     6.9852
Ex 2.10 sigma  2.5850     2.5850
P2.39 mu       9.7781     9.7781
P2.39 sigma    1.4448     1.4448
```

Truncation from below (Ex 2.11) and from above (P2.43), with
`truncated_distribution()`:

```{r}
#| label: truncated
cuts <- c(1000, 5000, 10000, 25000, 50000, 75000, 100000, 125000, 150000, 175000, 200000, Inf)
observed <- c(367, 112, 118, 65, 36, 13, 10, 8, 6, 4, 31)
f <- min_chi_square(function(m, s) truncated_distribution(lognormal(m, abs(s)), lower = 1000),
                    c(6.7, 2.7), cuts = cuts, observed = observed)
fitted <- truncated_distribution(lognormal(f$par[1], abs(f$par[2])), lower = 1000)
rows <- list(row("Ex 2.11 mu", 6.6916, f$par[1], 4), row("Ex 2.11 sigma", 2.6965, abs(f$par[2]), 4),
             row("Ex 2.11 chi-square", 4.691, f$value, 3))

f <- min_chi_square(function(m, s) truncated_distribution(lognormal(m, abs(s)), upper = 50000),
                    c(9.5, 1.1), cuts = 5000 * (0:10),
                    observed = c(104, 120, 81, 54, 45, 32, 26, 18, 12, 8))
rows <- c(rows, list(row("P2.43 mu", 9.495111, f$par[1], 4), row("P2.43 sigma", 1.084180, abs(f$par[2]), 4)))
book_table(rows, "Lognormals fitted by minimum chi-square to truncated samples",
           "Ex 2.11 (deductible 1,000, limit 200,000) and P2.43 (up to 50,000)")
```

```text
                      book  prospicio
Ex 2.11 mu          6.6916     6.6916
Ex 2.11 sigma       2.6965     2.6965
Ex 2.11 chi-square   4.691      4.691
P2.43 mu            9.4951     9.4951
P2.43 sigma         1.0842     1.0842
```

`severity_fit()` fits individual claims by maximum likelihood: the deductible is
a reporting threshold and the limit is censoring. The 20,000 draws equal the
Python guide's:

```{r}
#| label: fit
truth <- lognormal(6.6916, 2.6965)
ground_up <- draws(truth, 20000, seed = 2)
kept <- ground_up[ground_up > 1000]
recorded <- pmin(kept, 200000)
at_limit <- kept >= 200000
cat(sprintf("%s of 20,000 claims recorded, %d at the limit\n", num(length(kept)), sum(at_limit)))
```

```text
9,551 of 20,000 claims recorded, 415 at the limit
```

```{r}
#| label: fit-table
fits <- list(
  "ignoring both" = severity_fit("lognormal", recorded),
  "censoring only" = severity_fit("lognormal", recorded, censored = at_limit),
  "truncation and censoring" = severity_fit("lognormal", recorded, censored = at_limit,
                                            reporting_thresholds = rep(1000, length(kept)))
)
frame <- data.frame(
  fit = names(fits),
  mu = unname(sapply(fits, function(f) f$parameters[["meanlog"]])),
  se = unname(sapply(fits, function(f) f$standard_errors[["meanlog"]])),
  sigma = unname(sapply(fits, function(f) f$parameters[["sdlog"]]))
)
gt(frame, rowname_col = "fit") |>
  tab_header("Ex 2.11 refitted from the 20,000 simulated claims", "The population has mu 6.69 and sigma 2.70") |>
  cols_label(se = "se of mu") |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(mu, se, sigma), decimals = 2)
```

```text
                            mu  se of mu  sigma
ignoring both             8.94      0.01   1.46
censoring only            8.96      0.02   1.52
truncation and censoring  6.76      0.15   2.67
```

On a log scale: the 20,000 ground-up claims (never seen), the recorded ones, and
each fit's expected count per bin:

```{r}
#| label: fit-figure
edges <- 10^((0:70) / 10)                               # 1 to 10,000,000, ten bins a decade
shown <- list("fit ignoring both" = fits[["ignoring both"]],
              "fit with both" = fits[["truncation and censoring"]])
steps <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(shown), function(label) {
  p <- shown[[label]]$parameters
  counts <- 20000 * diff(cdf(lognormal(p[["meanlog"]], p[["sdlog"]]), edges))
  data.frame(fit = label, size = edges, claims = c(counts, counts[length(counts)]))
}))
ggplot() +
  geom_histogram(aes(size, fill = "ground-up"), data = data.frame(size = ground_up),
                 breaks = edges) +
  geom_histogram(aes(size, fill = "recorded"), data = data.frame(size = recorded),
                 breaks = edges) +
  geom_step(aes(size, claims, colour = fit), data = steps, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(1000, 200000), colour = "grey40", linetype = "dotted") +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("ground-up" = "grey82", "recorded" = "grey55")) +
  labs(x = "claim size (dotted: the deductible and the limit)", y = "claims in the bin",
       fill = NULL, colour = NULL,
       title = "Ex 2.11: only the corrected fit follows the population") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

book_table(rows, "Mean excess at 3,000 (P5.2) and the Pareto fitted by regression (Ex 5.4)")

Ex 5.8 and P5.10: CVs of the lognormal (5.9809; 1.8) and its layers. The
monograph's differences of rounded limited means cause the differences in the
third and fourth figures; the rounded-inputs row reproduces its layer CV:

```{r}
#| label: ex58
ln <- lognormal(5.9809, 1.8)
s3 <- surv(ln, 3000)
layer_mean <- layer(ln, 5000, 3000) / s3
layer_m2 <- layer_second_moment(ln, 5000, 3000) / s3
cv_limited <- function(l) sqrt(limited_second_moment(ln, l) - lev(ln, l)^2) / lev(ln, l)
m <- (1276 - 891) / 0.130239
m2 <- (5774970 - 1853050 - 2 * 3000 * (1276 - 891)) / 0.130239
book_table(list(
  row("Ex 5.8 F(3,000)", 0.869761, cdf(ln, 3000), 6),
  row("E[X; 3,000]", 891, lev(ln, 3000)),
  row("E[X^2; 3,000]", 1853050, limited_second_moment(ln, 3000)),
  row("E[X^2; 8,000]", 5774970, limited_second_moment(ln, 8000)),
  row("CV[X]", 4.9531, sqrt(variance(ln)) / mean(ln), 4),
  row("E[X_3K], the excess mean", 8515, stop_loss(ln, 3000) / s3),
  row("CV of the layer 5K xs 3K", 0.6452, sqrt(layer_m2 - layer_mean^2) / layer_mean, 4),
  row("same, from the book's rounded inputs", 0.6452, sqrt(m2 - m * m) / m, 4),
  row("P5.10 CV[X; 3,000]", 1.1551, cv_limited(3000), 4),
  row("P5.10 CV[X; 8,000]", 1.5959, cv_limited(8000), 4)
), "Moments and CVs of the lognormal (5.9809; 1.8)")
```

P5.12: a policy with a 100 deductible and a 3,000 limit, Pareto (3; 5,000),
5 ground-up claims:

```{r}
#| label: p512
p <- shifted_pareto(3, 5000)
shares <- severities <- losses <- numeric()
for (L in list(c(0, 100), c(100, 2900), c(3000, Inf))) {
  reach <- survival(p, L[1])
  loss <- if (is.infinite(L[2])) stop_loss(p, L[1]) else layer(p, L[2], L[1])
  shares <- c(shares, reach)
  severities <- c(severities, loss / reach)
  losses <- c(losses, 5 * loss)
}
grid_table("layer", c("[0; 100]", "(100; 3,000]", "(3,000; inf)", "total, 5 x mean"), list(
  list("share reaching", c(1.0000, 0.9423, 0.2441, NA), c(shares, NA), 4),
  list("severity", c(97.08, 1513.66, 4000.00, NA), c(severities, NA), 2),
  list("expected loss", c(485, 7132, 4883, 12500), c(losses, sum(losses)), 0)
), "P5.12: three layers of a policy with a 100 deductible and a 3,000 limit")
```

## 7. Inflation above an attachment: the leveraging effect

```{r}
#| label: leverage
p <- shifted_pareto(2, 3000); t <- 1.10
e0 <- stop_loss(p, 5000) / survival(p, 5000)
e1 <- t * stop_loss(p, 5000 / t) / survival(p, 5000 / t)
layer0 <- layer(p, 4000, 5000) / survival(p, 5000)
layer1 <- t * layer(p, 4000 / t, 5000 / t) / survival(p, 5000 / t)
count <- survival(p, 5000 / t) / survival(p, 5000)
book_table(list(
  row("Ex 5.10 e(5,000)", 8000, e0),
  row("e(5,000) after inflation", 8300, e1),
  row("excess severity trend, %", 3.75, 100 * (e1 / e0 - 1), 2),
  row("layer 4K xs 5K severity, trended", 2701, layer1),
  row("layer severity trend, %", 1.27, 100 * (layer1 / layer0 - 1), 2),
  row("Ex 5.11 excess count factor", 1.1241, count, 4),
  row("Ex 5.12 excess count trend, %", 18.03, 100 * (1.05 * count - 1), 2),
  row("excess loss trend, %", 22.46, 100 * (1.05 * count * e1 / e0 - 1), 2),
  row("of which from claim size, %", 16.6, 100 * (count * e1 / e0 - 1), 1)
), "Ex 5.10 to 5.12: 10% inflation on the layer above 5,000")
```

}
for (case in list(c(2000, 9.5), c(5000, 10.2))) {

                           100 * (t * layer(ln, case[1] / t, 3000 / t) / layer(ln, case[1], 3000) - 1), 1)))
}
book_table(rows, "P5.1, P5.21 and P5.22: severity, count and loss trends", "10% inflation")

## 9. Risk loads

```{r}
#| label: risk-load
sd_load <- function(sev, l, k, delta) k * sqrt(limited_second_moment(sev, l) + delta * lev(sev, l)^2)
var_load <- function(sev, l, k, delta) k * (limited_second_moment(sev, l) + delta * lev(sev, l)^2)
loaded_ilf <- function(sev, l, base, k, delta, load = sd_load, u = 0.2) {
  premium <- function(x) (1 + u) * lev(sev, x) + load(sev, x, k, delta)
  premium(l) / premium(base)
}
loaded <- sapply(limits, function(l) loaded_ilf(ln, l, b, 0.0277, 0))
grid_table("limit", limits, list(
  list("load rho(l)", c(627, 1473, 2013, 2663, 3090, 3410, 3668),
       sapply(limits, function(l) sd_load(ln, l, 0.0277, 0)), 0),
  list("loaded I(l)", c(1.0, 1.5770, 1.8074, 2.0128, 2.1197, 2.1897, 2.2407), loaded, 4)
), "Ex 6.5: the standard deviation load")
```

## 10. Deductibles

```{r}
#| label: deductibles
base <- lev(ln, b)
deds <- c(1000, 2000, 3000, 4000, 5000, 10000)
dlev <- sapply(deds, function(d) lev(ln, d))
straight <- dlev / base
franchise <- (dlev - deds * surv(ln, deds)) / base
diminishing <- (dlev - deds * (sapply(deds + 1000, function(d) lev(ln, d)) - dlev) / 1000) / base
grid_table("deductible", deds, list(
  list("C(d), straight", c(0.0741, 0.1249, 0.1661, 0.2016, 0.2328, 0.3534), straight, 4),
  list("frequency x 10^6", c(258, 201, 169, 147, 132, 89), 1e6 * 0.0005 * surv(ln, deds), 0),
  list("pure premium", c(4.942, 4.671, 4.451, 4.262, 4.095, 3.451), 0.0005 * 1.2 * (base - dlev), 3)
), "Ex 6.7: the straight deductible")
```

```{r}
#| label: p613
losses <- c(1000, 1550, 1700, 2200, 2500, 3000, 5200, 9000, 11000, 12500, 15000, 19800)
rows <- list()
for (case in list(list("P6.13", 20000, c(62200, 0.2635, 80200, 0.0503)),
                  list("P6.14", 12000, c(50900, 0.3973, 68900, 0.1841)))) {
  capped <- pmin(losses, case[[2]])
  paid_straight <- sum(pmax(capped - 2000, 0))
  paid_franchise <- sum(capped[losses > 2000])
  bk <- case[[3]]
  rows <- c(rows, list(
    row(paste(case[[1]], "straight: insurer pays"), bk[1], paid_straight),
    row(paste(case[[1]], "straight: LER"), bk[2], 1 - paid_straight / sum(losses), 4),
    row(paste(case[[1]], "franchise: insurer pays"), bk[3], paid_franchise),
    row(paste(case[[1]], "franchise: LER"), bk[4], 1 - paid_franchise / sum(losses), 4)))
}
book_table(rows, "P6.13 and P6.14: deductibles on twelve actual losses")
```

P6.17: a Pareto (3; 10,000), basic limit 5,000, frequency 0.005, e = 250:

```{r}
#| label: p617
p <- shifted_pareto(3, 10000)
deds2 <- c(0, 250, 500, 750, 1000)
plev <- sapply(deds2, function(d) lev(p, d))
base2 <- lev(p, 5000) + 250
grid_table("deductible", deds2, list(
  list("C(d), straight", c(0.0, 0.0855, 0.1648, 0.2385, 0.3071), (plev + 250 * cdf(p, deds2)) / base2, 4),
  list("pure premium", c(15.139, 13.845, 12.644, 11.528, 10.489),
       0.005 * (base2 - plev - 250 * cdf(p, deds2)), 3),
  list("C(d), franchise", c(NA, 0.0088, 0.0221, 0.0391, 0.0590),
       c(NA, ((plev - deds2 * survival(p, deds2) + 250 * cdf(p, deds2)) / base2)[-1]), 4)
), "P6.17: a Pareto (3; 10,000) with a fixed ALAE of 250")
```

Ex 6.10, inflation on a deductible of 500, without a limit and with a 5,000 limit:

```{r}
#| label: ex610
pure_premium <- function(sev, top, d, e, phi = 0.25) {
  capped <- if (is.null(top)) mean(sev) else lev(sev, top)
  phi * (capped - lev(sev, d) + surv(sev, d) * e)
}
now <- shifted_pareto(2, 8000); later <- shifted_pareto(2, 8400)
rows <- list()
for (case in list(list(NULL, c(1893, 1994, 5.3), 0, "no limit"),
                  list(5000, c(662.7, 677.3, 2.2), 1, "5,000 limit"))) {
  p0 <- pure_premium(now, case[[1]], 500, 50)
  p1 <- pure_premium(later, case[[1]], 500, 52.5)
  rows <- c(rows, list(row(paste0("Ex 6.10 ", case[[4]], ": pure premium"), case[[2]][1], p0, case[[3]]),
                       row("after 5% inflation", case[[2]][2], p1, case[[3]]),
                       row("effective trend, %", case[[2]][3], 100 * (p1 / p0 - 1), 1)))
}
book_table(rows, "Ex 6.10: inflation on a deductible of 500")
```

```text
                                    book  prospicio
Ex 6.10 no limit: pure premium     1,893      1,893
after 5% inflation                 1,994      1,994
effective trend, %                   5.3        5.3
Ex 6.10 5,000 limit: pure premium  662.7      662.7
after 5% inflation                 677.3      677.3
effective trend, %                   2.2        2.2
```
